items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: He was the chap I used to play with most of all before I joined the Johnson band.

ctx.x: We didn't want to, or we sort of didn't want to if it was going to affect his relatives at all. You know, they didn't know anything about jazz. But, his wife insisted. Mm-hmm. So, we did it. They were very happy about it. Happy. They were very glad we did it. Mm-hmm.
And what about John's sewing stuff?

He was the chap I used to play with most of all before I joined the Johnson band. Mm-hmm. He is a very keen cornet player. But, he was rough. He was pretty awful for a while. I can remember playing with him and thinking, oh, gosh, this is no value at all. He's so far off. He's sort of very keen, but he just can't get it. Suddenly, it all came. Obviously, he'd been practicing and thinking about it, but these things take time. Suddenly, it all sort of came to his fingertips and the 1948 Jazz Convention, he suddenly…
